purpose: Test whether an eight-iteration turn solve can improve the validated two-iteration continual-resolving leader while protecting every board-compatible opponent hand against the exact served two-iteration turn plus on-reach river anchor.

comparison.interpretation: The protected deeper turn policy slightly improved the first responder-zero value but materially worsened the second. Both responder-one values were bit-for-bit unchanged, so this mechanism cannot address the dominant remaining responder-one leak. Do not tune more turn iterations from this branch.

implementationEvidence.anchorParity: The protected anchor composes stabilized two-iteration turn rows with a separately solved two-iteration river policy on every exact propagated river range, matching runtime continual-resolver semantics.
implementationEvidence.safety: Every accepted generation is checked against an exact per-private-hand opponent best response and projected toward its anchor until maximum opponent CFV excess is at most 0.05bb.
implementationEvidence.routing: One atomic generation contains the resolving actor and frozen anchor opponent through the river; missing protected descendants fail closed and evaluator workers use isolated caches.
implementationEvidence.regression: short_turn_anchor_replays_the_configured_river_resolver invokes the exact safe solver and byte-compares the independently solved river continuation on a replayed turn line.

releaseGate.reason: The two-deal directional mean is above the release gate and is worse than the validated leader. Two deals are not sufficient evidence for a release confidence bound.

nextExperiment: Target the unchanged responder-one leak with a bilateral, anchor-consistent flop policy update; retain the 1.4127416606284693 leader and keep activation disabled.
